tagline: The 'town of a hundred islands' on the Gulf of Thailand — gateway to Samui, Cheow Lan Lake, and the old temple town of Chaiya
introHtml:
Surat Thani is one of the big provinces on the Gulf side of southern Thailand. Most people know it as the jumping-off point for Koh Samui, Koh Phangan, and Koh Tao — boats leave Don Sak and Surat Thani piers for the islands every day. But the province itself is more than a place you pass through: there's Cheow Lan Lake, often called the Guilin of Thailand, the Tapi River running through town, and Chaiya, an old archaeological town with deep history.

In the city you'll find riverside markets, the city pillar shrine, and restaurants along the Tapi River that are easy places to sit and eat. If you're into nature, head into Khao Sok to stay in a floating raft house on the lake and paddle past limestone cliffs. People come to Surat Thani to catch boats out to the islands, to get into the Khao Sok rainforest, and to stop by the Chaiya stupa and pick up the famous Chaiya salted eggs.
bestTime: January–April, clear skies and calm seas — good for boats out to Samui and Phangan and for trips to Cheow Lan Lake. The rainy season runs October–December.

highlights.name: Cheow Lan Lake and Khao Sok
highlights.blurb: A reservoir inside Khao Sok National Park where limestone cliffs rise straight out of emerald-green water — people call it the Guilin of Thailand. Sleeping in a raft house on the lake, paddling, and cruising for the views is the thing most people picture when they think of this province.

highlights.name: Gateway to Koh Samui, Phangan, Tao
highlights.blurb: Surat Thani is the connecting point for boats out to the Gulf islands. From Don Sak pier or the city you can catch a boat to Samui, Phangan, and Koh Tao every day. Most people pass through here before heading out to the islands.

highlights.name: Old Chaiya town and Phra Borommathat Chaiya
highlights.blurb: Chaiya is an ancient Srivijaya-era town, home to Phra Borommathat Chaiya, an old stupa revered by southerners, and an archaeological site that tells the story of the province's history.

highlights.name: Suan Mokkh
highlights.blurb: A forest meditation centre founded by Buddhadasa Bhikkhu at Chaiya. People walk through the 'Spiritual Theatre', look at the dharma-puzzle murals, and take in the quiet forest to sit and settle the mind.

highlights.name: Tapi River and riverside markets
highlights.blurb: The Tapi River runs through the middle of the city, with markets and restaurants along its banks. It's an easy place to stroll in the evening, eat by the water, and watch riverside life in Surat Thani.

highlights.name: Chaiya salted eggs
highlights.blurb: Salted eggs packed in termite-mound clay from Chaiya district — the yolk turns rich and sandy, salted just right. It's the province's signature take-home gift, something almost everyone buys on the way out.

foodScene.name: Gulf seafood
foodScene.note: Right on the Gulf and with fishing piers, the province has fresh prawns, shellfish, crab, fish, and oysters. Seafood spots in town and around Don Sak do it steamed, grilled, stir-fried, or in tom yum.

foodScene.name: Chaiya salted eggs
foodScene.note: The province's best-known specialty — salted eggs packed in termite-mound clay from Chaiya, with a rich, sandy yolk. Eat them with rice congee or buy a batch to take home.

foodScene.name: Bold southern Thai food
foodScene.note: Gaeng tai pla, gaeng leuang, khua kling, and stir-fried sator with prawns, eaten with hot steamed rice and fresh raw vegetables — local meals you can find all over town.

foodScene.name: Khanom jeen nam ya pak tai
foodScene.note: A popular breakfast and lunch — fermented rice noodles with a punchy southern fish curry, eaten with a spread of fresh raw vegetables: yard-long beans, pennywort, and cashew shoots.

foodScene.name: Khao yam pak tai
foodScene.note: Rice tossed with budu sauce, shredded vegetables, toasted coconut, and dried shrimp — sour, salty, and sweet balanced in one plate. A light meal southerners eat all the time.

foodScene.name: Surat Thani oysters
foodScene.note: Around Kanchanadit and Don Sak they farm big, meaty oysters — eaten raw with condiments or battered and fried. A standout along the Gulf coast.

foodScene.name: Coffee and cafes in town
foodScene.note: The city centre and the Tapi riverfront have laid-back cafes, from fresh-coffee shops to easy spots to hang out. A good place to grab a coffee while waiting for a boat or wandering the city.

foodScene.name: Surat Thani souvenirs
foodScene.note: Besides Chaiya salted eggs, there's Rongrian rambutan from Ban Na San — the origin of this variety — plus processed seafood and southern chili pastes to take home.

attractions.name: Khao Sok National Park and Cheow Lan Lake
attractions.blurb: An old rainforest with a reservoir where limestone cliffs rise out of emerald water. You can stay in a raft house, paddle a kayak, cruise for the views, and hike to caves.

attractions.name: Phra Borommathat Chaiya
attractions.blurb: An old Srivijaya-era stupa at Chaiya and an important sacred site for the south. People come to make merit and see the ancient architecture that's tied to the province.

attractions.name: Suan Mokkh
attractions.blurb: Buddhadasa Bhikkhu's forest meditation centre at Chaiya. Walk through the 'Spiritual Theatre', look at the dharma-puzzle murals, and sit quietly in the forest.

attractions.name: Don Sak Pier
attractions.blurb: The main pier where people catch ferries and speedboats to Koh Samui and Koh Phangan, with seafood restaurants and a market to stop at before boarding.

attractions.name: Tapi River and riverside markets in town
attractions.blurb: The main river running through the middle of the city, with markets, restaurants, and an evening walking path along its banks where you can see local riverside life.

attractions.name: Waterfalls and caves in the Khao Sok area
attractions.blurb: Beyond the lake, the Khao Sok area has river-cut caves, clear streams, and hiking trails through dense rainforest — good for people who like rougher, hands-on nature.

attractions.name: Koh Nok Phao and Ban Don Bay
attractions.blurb: Ban Don Bay in front of the city is a shellfish-farming and fishing area, with small islands and a fishing-community way of life you can take a boat out to see close to town.

attractions.name: Rongrian rambutan in Ban Na San
attractions.blurb: Ban Na San district is the origin of Rongrian rambutan. In fruit season there are orchards where you can stop to taste and buy it fresh off the trees.
